Title: Catalog module loads under the PR platform-version requirement
Preconditions: Platform image tag 3.1059.0-pr-3099-da0b-vcst-5387-top-level-catalog-assets; VirtoCommerce.Catalog 3.1041.0-pr-904-ce58; VirtoCommerce.BackupRestore 3.1004.0-pr-5-2048 deployed on {{BACK_URL}}

2. [HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/modules with the bearer token
3. [STATUS] Read the VirtoCommerce.Catalog and VirtoCommerce.BackupRestore entries: version, isInstalled, validationErrors
4. [ADMIN] Open the Admin SPA and confirm the Catalog and Backup/Restore menu items render
Assertions:
{OBSERVED} VirtoCommerce.Catalog reported version 3.1042.0-pr-904-2bfa and VirtoCommerce.BackupRestore reported 3.1004.0-pr-5-2048, both isInstalled=true with errors=[] and validationErrors=[].

Assertions:

Preconditions: A crafted Catalog backup whose binaryDataReference values are unsafe package paths
Steps:
1. [SETUP] Craft a Catalog backup whose binaryDataReference is each of: assets/../evil.txt | assets/./x.jpg | a backslash form assets\evil.jpg | evil/x.jpg with no assets/ prefix | assets/ with an empty relative path | a reference containing a control character
2. [ADMIN] Attempt to restore each crafted backup with Binary enabled
3. [STATUS] Record the error surfaced for each unsafe reference
4. [FILE] Inspect blob storage for any file written outside the intended asset root
Assertions:
{OBSERVED} All seven unsafe references were rejected, each error naming the offending value: assets/../evil, assets/./evil, a backslash form, a missing assets/ prefix, an empty relative path and a control character were refused as "not a safe package path"; the percent-encoded traversal assets/a%2F..%2F..%2F was caught by a second guard reporting it does not match the destination URL.

References: VCST-5387; BinaryDataEntryPath.Validate; CatalogPackageFormat.IsValidBinaryDataReference; Verified: VCST-5387 (2026-08-19, vcptcore-qa1)

Title: Export memory stays bounded for a large asset
Preconditions: A fixture asset of at least 200 MB attached to a product; a way to observe platform memory
Steps:
1. [STATUS] Record baseline platform working-set and managed-heap before the export
2. [ADMIN] Create a backup with Binary enabled including the large asset
3. [STATUS] Sample platform memory at short intervals during the export
4. [MATH] Compare the peak memory delta against the asset size
Assertions:
{OBSERVED} Five back-to-back binary exports pushed 900 MiB of incompressible assets (deflate ratio 1.0003) in 3.5 minutes; the executing pod went 559 -> 559 MiB with a peak excursion of about 4 MiB, while buffering would have reached ~1.4 GiB by run 5.
{OBSERVED} No OutOfMemoryException and no container restart; the pod also fell back from its peak (563 -> 553 -> 559 MiB), showing the plateau is retained GC heap plus page cache rather than a leak.
Cross_Layer_Checks: Grafana workload vcptcore-qa1-platform, per-pod series (two replicas; a deployment average would halve the spike). 4 GiB limit at ~520-560 MiB usage, so an OOM was never the detector — the graph delta is.
Failure_Signals: Memory delta approximates or exceeds the asset size; OOM; container OOMKilled; export times out
References: VCST-5387; story goal of bounded predictable memory; QA step 11 of comment 2026-08-11; Verified: VCST-5387 (2026-08-19, vcptcore-qa1)

Assertions:

{OBSERVED} Both 90 MiB assets restored byte-identical by SHA256 after being deleted (confirmed HTTP 404 first).
Cross_Layer_Checks: Grafana per-pod series identified the executing replica by its footprint: the green pod moved +33 MiB while the other moved +3 MiB.
Failure_Signals: Memory delta approximates the asset size; OOM during restore; checksum mismatch after a streamed restore
References: VCST-5387; story goal of bounded predictable memory; QA step 11 of comment 2026-08-11; Verified: VCST-5387 (2026-08-19, vcptcore-qa1)
